title: CI_CD In 5 Minutes _ Is It Worth The Hassle

segments.text: What is CICD? How does it help us ship faster? Is it worth the hassle? Let's take a look.
CICD or continuous integration and continuous delivery all make the software development
process from the initial code commit all the way through to deployment. It eliminates
much of the manual human intervention traditionally required to get new code to production.
The CICD process takes care of building, testing, and deploying new code to production.
The promise is that it enables software teams to deploy better quality software faster.
Now, this all sounds very good but does it work in real life? What the answer is? It depends.
Let's break up CICD into their own ports and discuss them separately.
CICD's less controversial and more common. In a nutshell, it is the practice of using
automation to enable teams to merge code changes into the share repository early and
often. Each commit triggers an automated workflow on a CICD server that runs a series of tasks
to make sure the commit is safe to merge into the main branch. It goes CICD process relies on a
good set of tests. It is not trivial to maintain a set of tests with sufficient coverage
and that are not flaky. High test coverage usually takes longer to run. This impacts developer
productivity. It is a tough balancing act but it's worth the effort to get it right.
What are some common tools used in CI? A good source code management system is the foundation.
Get help is a very popular example. You should hold everything needed to build a software.
This includes source code, test scripts, and script to build a software applications.
There are many tools to manage the CI process itself. Get up actions and build
height are some modern examples. Jenkins, Circle CI, and Travis CI are also common.
These tools manage the bill and test tasks in CI. There are many test tools for writing and
running tests. These tools are usually language and ecosystem specific. For example,
for JavaScript, Jess is an example of the unit testing framework, while playwright and cypress
are some common integration testing frameworks for web applications. The bill tools are even
more diverse and ecosystem specific. Greater is a powerful bill tool for Java. The JavaScript
bill ecosystem is fragmented, and how to keep track of. Webpack is the standard, but many new
bill tools claim to be much faster, but they are not yet as extensible as webpack.
Now let's examine the CD part of CI CD. CD is continuous deployment. Now it will be
truthful. Real continuous deployment is hard. They do exist, but the practice is not as common as CI.
Many teams only practice CD on the most basic types of systems. These systems are usually
stailers, like the API or web server tiers. With good production monitoring, these systems
could be deployed continuously with minimal risks. They are stailers and rollbacks are usually
quick and harmless. It's also a common practice to grab new features in feature flags
to separate a deployment of the code from the activation of the features. This allows the
team to quickly shut up new features if they cause any issues with that requiring a full
rollback. Canary deployment is also common practice for products with hundreds of millions of
users. It applies to a new production code to a tiny subset of the power users and staff
who both appreciate new features and have the risk appetite to help catch problems
before the new code is deployed widely. This allows the team to test the new code in a real
world environment while limiting the blast radius if something goes wrong. These techniques work
well for simple stailers systems. On the other hand, very few teams have the resources
or the convictions to implement real continuous hand-off deployments on complex
stailers systems like database back and clusters or other types of stailers systems
like web socket clusters. Instead, these systems are usually on a fixed deploy cadence.
The deployment process is manual, risky and time consuming. They require the care of a
dedicated platform team. It is rare to see these systems deploy fully continuously and automatically.
Now, what are some tools that are used for CD? The tools we mentioned earlier like GitHub
actions, built-kai and Jenkins are commonly used to handle CD tests. There are also the
infrastructure specific tools that make CD easier to maintain. For example, on Kubernetes,
Oracle CD is popular. In conclusion, CICD is a powerful software development practice that can
help teams ship better quality software faster. However, it is not a one-size-fits-all solution,
and its implementation may vary depending on the complexity of the system. If you like to learn
more about system design, check out our books and weekly newsletter. Please subscribe if you learned
something new. Thank you so much and we'll see you next time.
